BiblicalUsage: I is the longer form of the Hebrew pronoun, the word Moses, David, and the prophets use when they speak of themselves before God. I am the LORD thy God, I am a worm and no man, I will sing unto the LORD: the word is only a pronoun, but the sentences built on it hold the whole of prayer and promise.
TheologicalSignificance: The longer I carries no doctrine by itself; its weight is in the mouths that use it, from God's I am the LORD to the psalmist's I am a worm.
